bullets.title: STX: Massive Beat-and-Raise; PT targets $1,187–$1,300; nearline allocated into CY28
bullets.body: Seagate crushed F4Q26 with revenue $3.63B vs. Street $3.50B, EPS $5.71 vs. $5.10, gross margin 52.7% vs. ~50.6% consensus. F1Q27 guide $4.0–4.2B revenue and $7.10–7.50 EPS towers above prior consensus of $3.77B/$5.89. All major nearline capacity is allocated into CY28 with customer planning extending to CY29+; pricing +20% YoY expected in F1Q27. JPM raised PT to $1,240, Citi to $1,300 (Buy), Morgan Stanley to $1,187; UBS stays Neutral at $860 viewing the story as cyclical.

bullets.title: MSFT & META reporting tonight; MSFT sentiment worst in Mag7, META down 9 straight days
bullets.body: Both report after close Wednesday with AI capex the focal point: MSFT investor median capex expectation ~$260B FY27; must show tangible Copilot/LLM progress to reverse weak momentum. META has declined nine consecutive days (longest streak in company history) and is expected to guide capex higher for 2026; upside to Q2 revenue likely. JPM flags MSFT as having worst sentiment in Mag7.

bullets.title: KLAC: Beat-and-raise but below elevated buy-side bar; WFE raised to low-$150B; stock -8% premarket
bullets.body: KLA reported F4Q26 revenue $3.66B (+1.4% above consensus) and guided F1Q27 to $4.0B midpoint, roughly in line with Street but below the ~$4.05B buy-side bar. CY26 WFE raised to low-$150B (~25% growth) with advanced packaging up 70%+ in CY26. Gross margin guidance ~62.5% for CY26. Citi maintains Buy at $290; JPM and Morgan Stanley cut PTs to $238 and $253 respectively; UBS cuts to $215 (Neutral) on tepid margin commentary and INTC pull-forward risk.

bullets.title: GLW: 2Q below buy-side on carrier weakness and margin miss; multiple PT cuts; BofA removes from US 1 List
bullets.body: Corning's optical enterprise grew 65% YoY with Gen AI sales nearly doubling, but optical margin reached only 21.2% vs. elevated expectations and carrier revenue grew just 1% YoY vs. 36% in Q1. 3Q guidance revenue $4.95B slightly below consensus $5.0B. Morgan Stanley cuts PT to $165 (EW), JPM to $170 (OW), Mizuho to $210; BofA removed GLW from its US 1 List. UBS flags elevated capex (~$2B in '26, ~$2.5B in '27) as concern.

bullets.title: BE: First $1B quarter; FY guidance raised ~$450M; PT cut to $225 on multiple compression
bullets.body: Bloom Energy delivered its first-ever $1B revenue quarter in Q2 and raised FY26 revenue guidance to $3.9–4.2B (from $3.4–3.8B), boosting profit guidance by $175M (+26%). Qualified with all major US hyperscalers and dozen+ neo-clouds. Roth cuts PT to $225 from $285 on sector multiple contraction; Morgan Stanley maintains OW at $310 noting scandium supply concerns addressed. Stock was up ~8–10% after hours despite a 39% decline from June highs.

bullets.title: CLS: Monster beat-and-raise; 2027 guidance raised to +65% growth; Wolfe PT $475
bullets.body: Celestica reported Q2 revenue $4.7B vs. Street $4.4B, with 2026 revenue guidance raised to $20.5B (+65% YoY) and 2027 expected to grow a further 65%+. OpenAI next-gen rack and AMD Scale-Up switching programs ramp 1H'27, each contributing multiple billions. JPM raised PT to $485 (OW); Wolfe Research raised to $475 (OP). EPS $2.54 beat $2.30 consensus.

bullets.title: VRT: Disappoints; -15% premarket on weak beat
bullets.body: Vertiv was cited across multiple morning notes as a notable earnings miss/weak beat, down 15.1% in premarket trading. No detailed note in the digest but named alongside CAR as the session's standout downside surprises vs. BE and STX on the upside.

bullets.title: ALAB: PT raised to $315; Trainium3 content growing 5x vs T2 by end-2026
bullets.body: Citi raises ALAB PT to $315 on strong Trainium3 content per compute dollar with Amazon (~$600+/T3 vs. T3 Trainium2 base), agentic CPU and CXL memory positioning, and Scorpio/Helios ramp. FY26/27/28 EPS raised 5%/15%/24%. Citi flags key earnings questions: Scorpio UALINK traction, Helios content update, and TAM from CXL retimers. Maintains Buy.

bullets.title: MRVL: $250M India investment; optical engineering contact flags data center architecture rethink
bullets.body: Marvell announced a $250M investment in India over three years focused on AI, cloud, and data infrastructure semiconductor design. Separately, a contact at Marvell's optical engineering team (SVP/CTO level) is proposing an alternative to large campus-based data center buildout centered on interconnect/networking solutions.

bullets.title: NXPI: In-line beat and raise; auto upside disappoints relative to TXN; Wolfe PT $330
bullets.body: NXP reported Q2 revenue $3.50B beat ($3.47B est), Q3 guided $3.65–3.85B above $3.71B consensus. Industrial/IoT and Communications drove upside; auto +12% YoY but only slightly above consensus, causing disappointment vs. elevated expectations set by TXN. Citi maintains Buy $370; Wolfe raises to $330 (OP) citing cyclical upturn signals (lead times extending, rush orders 2x). Stock fell on lack of auto upside.

bullets.title: SWKS: Mixed F3Q; F4Q EPS guide misses on input cost pressure; dividend cut ahead of QRVO close
bullets.body: Skyworks F3Q revenue $935M beat consensus but F4Q EPS guidance $1.27 missed $1.29 consensus on rising input costs and higher interest expense from QRVO financing. Company cut its quarterly dividend to preserve cash for QRVO deal (expected to close by end of September). Citi cuts PT to $64, UBS raises to $70 (Neutral); mobile segment better than feared driven by Apple. QRVO in Phase 3 SAMR review.

bullets.title: ENPH: PT cuts across the board; FCC inverter ban a modest positive; residential solar still weak
bullets.body: Enphase reported Q2 in-line but US residential solar demand remains depressed (industry -30% YoY). FCC ban on foreign inverters adds a base-case 50MW opportunity ($15–90M incremental revenue). Mizuho cuts PT to $45 (-17%); Morgan Stanley maintains UW at $27; Roth maintains Buy at 14x 2027E EPS. Safe-harbor backlog strong through 2028–2030 but near-term US resi recovery delayed.

bullets.title: T: Closes $23B EchoStar spectrum deal, reaffirms all guidance
bullets.body: AT&T closed its $23B spectrum acquisition from EchoStar, adding approximately 50 MHz of low/mid-band spectrum across the US, strengthening its 5G and fiber position. Company reaffirmed all financial guidance following the deal close.

bullets.title: CHTR: JPM cuts PT to $150; broadband losses raised to 600k; 2026 EBITDA now expected to decline
bullets.body: Charter management shifted guidance to expect 2026 standalone EBITDA to decline ~1% YoY vs. prior expectation of slight growth. JPM raises 2026 broadband net losses to 600k on fiber overbuild, FWA, and emerging LEO satellite pressure and cuts PT to $150 from $200 (Neutral). Charter paused buybacks through Q3 and reduced leverage target. Cox deal expected to close late August.

bullets.title: DASH: Q2 GOV beat likely; margins not inflecting; 2027 EBITDA bull/bear debate is key
bullets.body: JPM Tech Sketch: DASH Q2 GOV likely to beat Street's $32.6B guide (alt data strong); however adj. EBITDA margin inflection not expected in Q2. Management guided 2H materially higher with Q3 approaching $1B EBITDA. 2027 EBITDA bull case >$5B vs. Street $4.7B depends on incremental margins reaching ~4–5% of GOV. Drone delivery expansion signaled by CEO tweet.

bullets.title: PLTR: Down 6% on channel checks showing competition and potential commercial slowdown
bullets.body: Palantir fell approximately 6% on channel checks suggesting increased competitive pressure, customer optimization, and possible commercial revenue growth deceleration. No fundamental detail change, but sentiment negative into Q2 report.

bullets.title: MU: Down sharply; unusual OTM call sweep of $3M+ spotted; Korea memory selloff contagion
bullets.body: Micron continues to fall amid the AI/memory selloff. A $3M+ OTM call sweep was detected (unusual options flow). JPM semis note flags Korea ETF unwind as ~90% complete and US semis basket now at 90th percentile from 98th percentile; positioning washout may be nearing end. Separate social accounts cited January recommendation near $350.

bullets.title: TXN: Arete Research upgrades to Buy, $405 PT (46% upside)
bullets.body: Arete Research upgraded Texas Instruments to Buy from Neutral with a $405 price target, implying approximately 46% upside from $277. FactSet average target stands at $325.

bullets.title: CRDO: Market misread Jensen's 'cableless' comment; Credo's external cabling business unaffected
bullets.body: Analysis clarifies that Nvidia's 'cableless' design refers to internal cables replaced by midplane PCB assembly, not external-to-rack cabling that Credo produces. The sell-off in CRDO was based on a misunderstanding; Nvidia telegraphed this design change months ago. Credo's external-rack interconnect business remains structurally intact.

bullets.title: Semis sector: -22.5% MTD, worst month since December 2002; positioning washout ~90% complete
bullets.body: Semiconductor stocks have declined 22.5% in July, on pace for the worst month since December 2002, driven by AI spending durability fears, SK Hynix earnings miss, KOSPI circuit breakers, and hedge fund deleveraging. JPM's Mixo Das notes levered ETF unwind ~90% complete. JPM tactically bullish; sector positioning now at typical -1.0z+ selldown that historically marks bottoms. Hyperscaler earnings (MSFT, META tonight; AAPL, AMZN Thursday) may establish floor.
